headline.caveat: letter of intent — no contract value; analysts estimate >$70B (>₩100T) of incremental demand for Samsung + SK Hynix combined through 2029

realized_to_date.caveat: LOI stage; production ramps and firm purchase orders not publicly quantified

nature_md: Oct 1, 2025 letter of intent ('Stargate Korea', signed around meetings between Sam Altman, Korea's president, and both chaebols): Samsung Electronics commits to ramp advanced memory (HBM and DRAM) production toward OpenAI's projected demand of up to 900,000 DRAM wafer starts per month **combined with SK Hynix** — roughly 40% of global DRAM output. Samsung affiliates go further than memory: Samsung SDS on enterprise AI/data centers, Samsung C&T and Samsung Heavy Industries on data-center design including floating data centers, plus two Stargate data centers in Korea. All of it is LOI, not contract — the analyst dollar figure carries **low confidence** and the wafer number is OpenAI's projected demand, not a firm order.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: No financial commitment recognized — an LOI creates no obligation. If converted to contracts, OpenAI (and Stargate partners) would carry enormous forward supply obligations, likely with prepayments, as is becoming standard in HBM.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Nothing bookable yet; the strategic value is capacity-planning cover for Samsung to expand wafer starts. Samsung is separately an investor in Anthropic's Series H — the Korean memory duopoly is financially entangled with both leading labs.

observations.metric_label: Projected DRAM wafer starts/month for OpenAI (Samsung + SK Hynix combined)
observations.notes: ≈40% of global DRAM output; OpenAI's stated demand projection, not a firm order. Analyst estimate of >$70B combined value through 2029 is single-sourced (KED Global) — low confidence.
